newsitem.title: CHINA: China crude imports seen at 34 mln T in '97 - paper.
newsitem.headline: China crude imports seen at 34 mln T in '97 - paper.

text.p: China's crude oil imports were expected to reach at least 34 million tonnes in 1997, taking a share of about 25 percent of total supply, the China Daily said on Tuesday.

The gap between domestic supply and demand was continuing to widen, the newspaper quoted Yang Wenfang, vice president of Sinochem International Oil Co, part of state importer China National Chemicals Import and Export Co (Sinochem), as saying.
Current oil imports account for 12 percent of demand, but the percentage is expected to rise in the next few years, Yang said.
He forecast imports in 1997 at 34 million tonnes.
Imports in 1996 amounted to 22 million tonnes, an increase of 37.5 percent from the previous year, Yang said.
Last week, customs figures reported by the Xinhua news agency showed China's 1996 imports of crude oil soared by 32 percent to 22.62 million tonnes.
China imported 17.09 million tonnes of crude in 1995, up by 38.4 percent from 1994. Exports in 1995 were 18.85 million tonnes, up by 1.5 percent year-on-year.
